question: The five functions of management in their accepted order are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Management begins with planning, moves through organising, staffing and directing, and ends with controlling, which measures whether the plan was achieved

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — directing, controlling, planning, organising and staffing: Directing can only follow a plan and a staff

C — staffing, directing, controlling, organising and planning: Staffing is chosen after the work has been organised

D — controlling, planning, staffing, directing and organising: Control comes last and cannot be placed before planning

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer who writes the plan first and keeps the control for the end works through the month in order, while one who starts by checking finds nothing to check against

question: Deciding in advance what is to be done, how and by whom is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. planning

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Planning is the step in which the goal, the method and the person responsible are decided before the work begins

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — supervision: Supervision guides the work while it is going on

B — evaluation: Evaluation judges the worth of what was done

D — controlling: Controlling compares the result with the plan

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: A nursing officer writes the plan for the day before the shift begins, because a ward that starts by reacting to whatever arrives loses the hours in which the planned care should have been given

question: Grouping the work of the ward into units and fixing the lines of authority among them is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. organising

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Organising divides the work into groups, sets the authority of each and links them into one structure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — staffing: Staffing fills the posts created by the structure

B — budgeting: Budgeting provides the money

D — recruiting: Recruiting is only the first step of staffing

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: A ward in which each nurse knows exactly which patients and which tasks are hers is an organised ward, and the confusion in the others comes from an unclear structure rather than from a shortage of staff

question: For a general medical ward of 30 beds the recommended nurse to patient ratio for the morning shift is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 1 nurse to 6 patients

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The usual norm for a general ward in the morning is about one nurse to every six patients, which allows the medicines, the rounds, the dressings and the documentation to be done

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1 nurse to 30 patients: One to thirty cannot even give the medicines safely

B — 1 nurse to 15 patients: One to fifteen is too thin for the morning work

D — 1 nurse to 3 patients: One to three belongs to a high dependency or intensive area

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who is asked to cover double the norm writes the fact in the duty register, because a shortage that is nowhere recorded becomes the staff shortage that the office later denies

question: Patient classification for staffing means grading patients by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the amount of nursing care each one needs

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Patients are grouped from those who need total care to those who need minimal care, and the nurse requirement is worked out from these groups

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the name of the consultant: The consultant's name does not decide the care load

C — the cost of their treatment: The cost of treatment has no bearing on the nursing hours

D — the day of admission: The day of admission does not decide the need

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer classifies the patients at the start of the shift, because a ward of thirty self caring patients and a ward of thirty dependent ones need very different numbers of nurses
option_1: the amount of nursing care each one needs

question: The main purpose of the duty roster is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. make sure that every shift has enough nurses of the right skill

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A roster spreads the available nurses over the shifts so that each shift has the numbers and the skills it needs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — reduce the wages bill: Saving money is not the purpose of the roster

C — give every nurse the same duties: Duties are given according to skill and not made equal for all

D — keep the same nurse on night duty every night: Fixed night duty for one nurse leads to fatigue and is against the aim

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The roster is put up well in advance and a request book is kept along with it, because a nurse who learns of her duty only a day earlier arranges neither her rest nor her journey
option_1: make sure that every shift has enough nurses of the right skill
option_4: keep the same nurse on night duty every night

question: In a hospital budget, the money spent on building and on equipment is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. capital expenditure

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Money spent on land, building and costly equipment gives a benefit over many years and is called capital expenditure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — revenue expenditure: Revenue expenditure is the routine running cost, such as salaries, drugs and linen

C — contingency: A contingency is the amount kept aside for the unforeseen

D — petty cash: Petty cash is the small amount kept for day to day purchases

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer lists the equipment she needs with the reason and the number, because a request without a reason is the one that is cut first when the budget is pressed

question: When a senior nurse asks a junior nurse to carry out a dressing and then checks that it has been done properly, this is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. delegation with follow up

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The task was handed to a person able to do it and the result was checked, which is delegation with follow up

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a breach of the patient's right: No right of the patient was breached

C — refusal of duty: Duty was not refused

D — an incident of negligence: Nothing wrong was done to the patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The senior nurse stays answerable for the task even after handing it over, which is why the checking step cannot be skipped

question: Comparing the nursing care actually given with the standard set for it is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. controlling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Controlling measures the work against the standard and corrects the difference

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — organising: Organising builds the structure

B — planning: Planning sets the standard in the first place

C — staffing: Staffing provides the people

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer keeps a simple audit of a few standards each month, because a standard that is never measured quietly slips to whatever is convenient

question: A nursing officer explains that the first step before starting a new ward round system is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. decide the purpose and the steps of the change

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Any change begins with a clear purpose and a step by step plan, so that the staff can see where they are going

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — buy new registers: Registers are an aid and not a beginning

B — wait for the next inspection: Waiting does not prepare anyone

C — tell the staff that the change is compulsory: A change forced without a reason is resisted quietly

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer explains the reason for the change to the group before it begins, because staff who understand why a step was added carry it out honestly when no one is watching
option_3: tell the staff that the change is compulsory
option_4: decide the purpose and the steps of the change

question: A 20 bed ward has only two nurses for the morning shift and an admission is waiting. The nursing officer's sound decision is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. set the priorities, care for the most ill first, inform the office about the shortage and accept the admission only after arranging the cover

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nursing officer decides the priority of care, reports the shortage and arranges additional help before taking on work that cannot be done safely

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — send one nurse home to balance the duty roster: Sending a nurse home worsens the shortage

C — accept the admission and leave the other patients unattended: An unsafe admission risks the patients already in the ward

D — refuse all admissions without telling anyone: A refusal that is not reported leaves the office and the patient without any answer

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in charge records the request for extra staff with the time, because a shortage that has been reported in writing is the only one the office can be expected to act upon
option_1: send one nurse home to balance the duty roster
option_2: set the priorities, care for the most ill first, inform the office about the shortage and accept the admission only after arranging the cover
option_3: accept the admission and leave the other patients unattended

question: Nursing research is best described as a systematic enquiry that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. seeks answers to questions that improve nursing practice

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Research is a planned and orderly search for answers that can change and improve the way nursing is practised

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — replaces clinical judgement at the bedside: Research supports clinical judgement and does not replace it

B — proves that the senior staff are always right: Research questions the accepted practice rather than defending persons

D — is done only to publish papers: Publication is a result and not the purpose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A nurse who reads one small study on the right way to fix a cannula and changes her own practice has already used the first fruit of research
option_2: proves that the senior staff are always right
option_3: seeks answers to questions that improve nursing practice

question: The first step of the research process is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. state the problem clearly

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The process begins with a clearly stated problem, because the question decides the design, the sample and the tools that follow

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — write the report: The report is written at the end

C — collect the data: Data cannot be collected before the question is settled

D — choose the sample: The sample is chosen after the design

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A question that is written in one clear sentence at the start keeps the whole study on the rails, while a vague one is discovered halfway through and cannot be repaired

question: A null hypothesis in a research study states that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. there is no relation between the variables being studied

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The null hypothesis says that there is no relation or no difference between the variables, and the study is done to see whether the data can reject it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the study has already failed: The null hypothesis is a formal statement and not a judgement on the study

B — the sample chosen is too small: The size of the sample is a matter of design and not of the hypothesis

C — the variables are strongly related to each other: A strong relation is what the alternative hypothesis claims

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse states both the null and the alternative hypothesis before collecting the data, because a claim chosen after the results are seen is not a scientific statement at all
option_3: the variables are strongly related to each other
option_4: there is no relation between the variables being studied

question: A review of literature in a research study is done to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. find out what is already known, so that the work is not repeated blindly

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Reading what others have already found tells the researcher what is known, what is disputed and where the gap lies

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — fill the pages of the report: Length is not the purpose

C — replace the collection of data: A review never replaces the data

D — satisfy the librarian: The librarian is not concerned with the study

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the review with a pencil and notes the methods used before, because a good method borrowed from another study is often stronger than a new one invented in a hurry
option_2: find out what is already known, so that the work is not repeated blindly

question: In a study of whether a new dressing reduces wound infection, the independent variable is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the type of dressing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The independent variable is the one that the researcher changes, which here is the type of dressing

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the size of the sample: The sample size is a part of the design

C — the age of the patient: The age of the patient is a characteristic that is recorded, not the change introduced

D — the wound infection: The wound infection is the outcome and is the dependent variable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse states which variable is changed and which is measured before the study begins, because a study that confuses the two reports a change that has no clear cause

question: A study that simply describes how many nurses in a hospital wash their hands between patients is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a descriptive study

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A study that observes and describes what exists, without introducing any change, is descriptive

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a clinical trial: A clinical trial tests a treatment

C — an experimental study: An experimental study introduces a change and compares the effect

D — a case control study: A case control study compares the ill with the well

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse begins with a descriptive study when little is known about a problem, because a clear picture of the present state is what suggests the question for the next study

question: When every member of the population has an equal chance of being picked for the study, the method is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. simple random sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Simple random sampling gives every member an equal chance, which is what makes the sample fair

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — quota sampling: Quota sampling fills set numbers in each group

B — convenience sampling: Convenience sampling takes whoever is easiest to reach

D — purposive sampling: Purposive sampling selects members that the researcher judges suitable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse draws the sample from a list with a table of random numbers, because a sample of the patients who happened to be present that morning is not the population and cannot be generalised

question: A questionnaire sent to a large number of nurses is most useful when:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the questions are short, clear and closed, so that the answers can be counted

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A written questionnaire suits short clear questions with fixed answers, because they can be answered without help and counted easily

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the questions need long explanations: Questions that need long explanations are better asked in an interview

B — the researcher wants to observe a procedure: Observation is a different method altogether

D — the sample is very small: A very small sample is better handled by interviews

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tries the questionnaire on a few colleagues first, because a question that two of them read in different ways will be misread by fifty
option_2: the researcher wants to observe a procedure
option_3: the questions are short, clear and closed, so that the answers can be counted

question: The value that appears most often in a set of observations is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. mode

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in the data

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — mean: The mean is the arithmetic average of all the values

C — median: The median is the middle value when the data are arranged in order

D — range: The range is the gap between the highest and the lowest value

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the mode when the question is which finding is commonest, because the mean of a skewed set can describe a patient who does not exist in the ward

question: A 45-year-old woman is invited to join a study on a new dressing and is given a full written explanation before she agrees. This step is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. informed consent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A full explanation of the purpose, the method, the risks and the right to withdraw, followed by a free agreement, is informed consent

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — coding of data: Coding protects the identity of the data

B — randomisation: Randomisation is the way the participants are allotted to groups

C — blinding: Blinding hides the treatment from the participant or the observer

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse takes the consent before any data are collected and keeps the form safely, because consent obtained after the fact is not consent at all and places the whole study in doubt

question: A researcher copies a paragraph from another paper without naming the source. This is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. plagiarism and professional misconduct

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Using another person's words without an acknowledgment is plagiarism and is a serious fault in academic and professional work

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an accepted practice in reports: It is not accepted practice anywhere

B — a fair summary: A fair summary is written in one's own words with the source named

D — a permitted quotation: A permitted quotation is placed in quotes and credited

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the source on the note card at the moment of reading, because a reference that was meant to be added later is the one that is usually left out

question: The code of ethics of the Indian Nursing Council is mainly:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a guide to the professional conduct expected of a nurse

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The code sets out the conduct expected of a nurse towards the patient, the profession, the colleagues and the public

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a list of the drugs a nurse may give: The list of drugs is decided by the drugs rules and the hospital policy

C — a price list of nursing services: It deals with conduct and not with charges

D — a record of the nurse's attendance: Attendance is kept in the duty register

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps a copy of the code in the ward and reads a clause at the monthly meeting, because a standard that is discussed openly is easier to follow than one that exists only in a file
option_1: a list of the drugs a nurse may give
option_2: a guide to the professional conduct expected of a nurse

question: A valid consent for a surgical operation must be:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. given by the patient freely after being told what the operation involves

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Consent must be given by the patient, who is of age and of sound mind, after an explanation of the nature and the risks, without any pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — obtained after the patient has been sedated: Sedation removes the capacity to consent

B — signed by the nurse in charge: The nurse witnesses or explains but does not give consent for the patient

D — taken from a relative who is present: A relative may consent only for a minor or for a patient who cannot consent

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sees that the consent is taken before the premedication, because a signature obtained after the sedative is given is worthless in law
option_1: obtained after the patient has been sedated
option_3: given by the patient freely after being told what the operation involves
option_4: taken from a relative who is present

question: A patient falls out of bed because the side rails were not raised as ordered. In law this is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. negligence

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Negligence is the failure to give the care that a reasonable nurse would have given, and the result here was an injury that could have been prevented

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — defamation: Defamation is damage to a person's reputation

B — assault: Assault is the threat of harm

C — battery: Battery is harm done without consent

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes plainly what she found and what she did, because the record made at the time is the strongest protection for the patient and the honest answer in any enquiry

question: A 60-year-old man is injured by a nurse's error while she is on duty. Under the law he may claim damages from the hospital as well as from the nurse. This is known as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. vicarious liability of the employer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An employer is answerable for the acts of the employees done in the course of their duty, and this is vicarious liability

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — criminal liability: Criminal liability arises only in certain grave acts

C — no liability of any kind: The wrong done to the patient does create liability

D — personal liability of the nurse alone: The nurse remains answerable as well

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records every order and every dose exactly, because in a claim it is the written record and not the memory that decides who was responsible

question: A nurse should not discuss a patient's illness in the lift or the canteen because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. it is a breach of the patient's right to confidentiality

🧠 Clinical Rationale: All that the nurse learns about a patient in the course of care is confidential and is shared only with those who need it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — only the ward round may discuss patients: Discussion is allowed where it serves care and not merely in the ward round

C — the canteen is noisy: Noise is not the reason

D — the lift is too small: The size of the lift is irrelevant

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse holds the discussion at the bedside or in the duty room and speaks only of what is needed, because a chance remark heard by a neighbour does damage that no apology can undo
option_1: it is a breach of the patient's right to confidentiality
option_2: only the ward round may discuss patients

question: A nurse gives a drug on a verbal order from a doctor. She must:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. record the drug, the dose and the time, and have the doctor sign the order as soon as possible

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A verbal order is written down at once with the drug, the dose and the time, and is countersigned by the doctor as soon as it can be done

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rely on her memory of the order: Memory is not a record

B — ask another nurse to sign as the doctor: No nurse may sign for a doctor

C — wait for the next round to confirm: Waiting leaves an unrecorded dose on the chart

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the order back aloud to the doctor before giving the drug, because a poor telephone line can turn fifteen into fifty
option_1: rely on her memory of the order
option_2: ask another nurse to sign as the doctor
option_3: wait for the next round to confirm
option_4: record the drug, the dose and the time, and have the doctor sign the order as soon as possible

question: The thread like structures in the nucleus of the cell that carry the genes are called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. chromosomes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The chromosomes are the thread like bodies that carry the genes, and a human body cell has forty six of them

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — gametes: A gamete is a germ cell such as the sperm or the ovum

B — genes: A gene is a small part of a chromosome

C — enzymes: An enzyme is a protein that speeds a reaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains the picture of the chromosomes to the parents in simple words, because a family that understands the word chromosome asks better questions at the next visit

question: When both parents are carriers of an autosomal recessive disease, the chance that each child will be affected is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. one in four

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Two carriers have one chance in four of passing on both faulty genes, and that child is affected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — no chance at all: There is a real chance, which is why the couple is counselled

B — three in four: Three in four is the chance that the child is not affected

C — one in two: One in two is the chance of a carrier child

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains the same risk for every pregnancy, because a couple who have had one healthy child often believe the next one must be safe too

question: Haemophilia is inherited as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. an X linked recessive trait

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The faulty gene lies on the X chromosome, so boys who receive it are affected while girls who have one copy are usually carriers

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an autosomal dominant trait: An autosomal dominant trait would affect both sexes equally in every generation

B — an autosomal recessive trait: An autosomal recessive trait would need both parents to carry it and would affect girls as often as boys

D — a trait carried on the Y chromosome: The gene is on the X and not the Y chromosome

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains to the mother of an affected boy that she may be a carrier even though she is healthy, because she needs this information before she plans the next pregnancy
option_4: a trait carried on the Y chromosome

question: Genetic counselling aims mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. give information and support so that the family can make its own decision

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Counselling gives the facts, the risks and the support, and the decision remains with the family

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — test only the father: Both parents are involved

B — compel a couple to stop having children: Counselling never compels

D — cure the genetic disease: Most genetic diseases cannot be cured by counselling

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse gives the information in a quiet room with time for questions, because the risk figures told in a busy corridor are the ones the family remembers wrongly
option_2: compel a couple to stop having children
option_3: give information and support so that the family can make its own decision

question: Karyotyping is the study of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the number and the structure of the chromosomes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A karyotype is a picture of the chromosomes in a cell, arranged in pairs to show their number and their structure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the enzymes in the blood: Enzyme studies are biochemical tests

B — the pattern of inheritance in a family tree: The study of the family tree is a pedigree analysis

C — the blood groups of the family: Blood grouping is a separate test

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains that the test needs living cells and one plain blood sample, because a sample sent into the wrong bottle cannot be cultured and the test has to be repeated
option_2: the pattern of inheritance in a family tree
option_4: the number and the structure of the chromosomes

question: A 34-year-old woman at 16 weeks of pregnancy is advised amniocentesis for a genetic study. The main risk that the nurse must explain is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. injury to the fetus or leakage of fluid that may lead to miscarriage

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The needle enters the bag of fluid, and the small but real risks are injury to the fetus and leakage leading to miscarriage or infection

🔍 Key Clues: 34-year-old | 16 weeks

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — there is no risk at all: Every invasive test carries some risk, however small

C — permanent loss of hearing: Hearing is not affected

D — a rise in the blood sugar: The blood sugar is not affected

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the pulse and the abdominal findings before and after the test, because bleeding or a leak that is noticed early can be managed before labour begins
option_2: injury to the fetus or leakage of fluid that may lead to miscarriage

question: The correct order of the nursing process is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nurse first collects the data, states the nursing diagnosis, plans the care, carries it out and then evaluates the result

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — evaluation, planning, assessment, diagnosis and implementation: Evaluation is the last step and not the first

B — diagnosis, assessment, planning, evaluation and implementation: Diagnosis cannot be made before the data are collected

C — planning, assessment, implementation, diagnosis and evaluation: Planning needs both the data and the diagnosis first

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse goes back to assessment whenever the evaluation shows that the aim was not met, because the process is a circle and not a straight line

question: The nurse records an observation in the chart immediately after taking it mainly because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a record made at the time is accurate and can be relied on later

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A note made at the moment of the observation is accurate and carries full value if the record is examined later

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the pen is handy at that time: Convenience is not the reason

B — the chart must look full: A chart is not filled for appearance

question: The number of member countries of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 8

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Association has eight member countries, namely Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 10: Ten is more than the true number

B — 6: Six was the number before Afghanistan joined

C — 12: Twelve is well above the true number

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Regional cooperation matters in health, and the nurse working in a border district follows the same immunisation and disease reporting rules as the neighbouring country so that an outbreak does not cross back and forth unnoticed

question: The smallest continent in the world is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Australia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Australia is the smallest continent, though it is also a country in itself

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Antarctica: Antarctica is larger than Australia and is a continent of ice with no permanent residents

C — Europe: Europe is larger than Australia

D — South America: South America is larger than Australia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse working in a remote area understands the idea of wide distances from such a fact, and plans the visits and the vaccine carrier so that a whole round is not spoilt by one long journey

question: The Ranji Trophy is associated with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. cricket

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Ranji Trophy is the first class domestic cricket championship of India

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — football: Football has the Santosh Trophy

C — badminton: Badminton has the Thomas and the Uber Cup

D — hockey: Hockey has the Dhyan Chand and the Beighton Cup

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses the sports page of the newspaper in the ward, because a patient who is helped to follow his own game passes the long hours of bed rest far more easily

question: The Dronacharya Award is given for excellence in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. coaching in sports

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Dronacharya Award honours coaches who have trained sportspersons to outstanding performance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — writing: Writing is honoured by the Sahitya Akademi and the Jnanpith awards

C — acting: Acting is honoured by the National Film Awards

D — medicine: Medicine is honoured by the National Florence Nightingale Award among others

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows that excellence comes from long training and not from one good day, and the same is true of a nurse who becomes skilled only after years at the bedside

question: World Environment Day is observed on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 5 June

🧠 Clinical Rationale: World Environment Day is observed on the fifth of June to draw attention to the protection of the environment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7 April: The seventh of April is World Health Day

B — 5 September: The fifth of September is Teacher's Day

D — 1 December: The first of December is World AIDS Day

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse links Environment Day with the hospital waste that is sorted and the water that is not wasted, because the health of the ward and the health of the surroundings are one and the same work

question: Which Article of the Constitution gives the citizen the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the fundamental rights?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Article 32

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of a fundamental right, and this is why it is called the heart and soul of the Constitution

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Article 14: Article 14 gives equality before the law

B — Article 19: Article 19 gives the six freedoms such as speech and movement

D — Article 21: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: A nurse who knows that a right has a remedy is less afraid to speak up for a patient, because a duty that is not recorded and reported is a duty that quietly disappears

question: The first Indian to travel into space was:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Rakesh Sharma

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rakesh Sharma went into space in 1984 aboard a Soviet spacecraft and was the first Indian to do so

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Kalpana Chawla: Kalpana Chawla was an Indian born astronaut who flew much later

C — Vikram Sarabhai: Vikram Sarabhai was the founder of the Indian space programme and not an astronaut

D — Sunita Williams: Sunita Williams is an astronaut of Indian origin and also later

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse working in a burns or a cancer unit can tell such a story to a tired patient, because a small piece of good news shared at the right moment lifts the whole bed

question: The Bhoodan movement was started by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Vinoba Bhave

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vinoba Bhave started the Bhoodan movement, in which land was asked for as a gift and given to the landless

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Raja Ram Mohan Roy: Raja Ram Mohan Roy worked against social evils much earlier

C — Mahatma Gandhi: Mahatma Gandhi led the freedom movement and was not the founder of this one

D — Jayaprakash Narayan: Jayaprakash Narayan took part in the movement and later led another

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who understands a village landholding understands why some families are far poorer than others, and this shapes the way the health advice is given to each household

question: The instrument used to check the purity of milk is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. lactometer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The lactometer measures the density of milk, and from it the amount of water added to it can be judged

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — hydrometer: A hydrometer measures the density of a liquid but this is the general name and not the milk instrument

C — barometer: A barometer measures the pressure of the air

D — thermometer: A thermometer measures temperature

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in a community setting shows the mother how the milk from a bottle of unknown quality is tested, because watered milk gives the baby far less nourishment than the family believes

question: The gas that green plants give out during photosynthesis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. oxygen

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The plant uses carbon dioxide to make its food and gives out oxygen as a result

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide is taken in and not given out

C — nitrogen: Nitrogen is not given out in this process

D — hydrogen: Hydrogen is not released as a gas

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains why the plants near a ward window are useful and why the windows must still be opened, because the oxygen in a closed room is used up by every person in it

question: The human skull is made up of about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 22 bones

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The skull is made up of about twenty two bones, of which eight form the cranium and the rest the face

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 32 bones: Thirty two is the number of permanent teeth and not of the skull bones

C — 12 bones: Twelve is fewer than the true number

D — 42 bones: Forty two is far more than the true number

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse learns the names of the skull bones before reading a head injury report, because a fracture line is described by the bone in which it lies

question: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. vitamin B1

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A lack of vitamin B1, or thiamine, causes beriberi, in which the nerves and the heart are affected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — vitamin C: A lack of vitamin C causes scurvy

C — vitamin A: A lack of vitamin A causes night blindness and dry eyes

D — vitamin D: A lack of vitamin D causes rickets

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse watches this in a patient who lives mainly on polished rice and who complains of tingling in the feet, because the early nerve signs come before the weakness and the swelling appear

question: The blood group that is called the universal donor is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. O negative

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Group O negative blood carries neither the A nor the B antigen nor the Rh antigen, so it can be given to almost any patient in an emergency

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A positive: A positive blood carries the A and the Rh antigens

B — B negative: B negative carries the B antigen

C — AB positive: AB positive is the universal recipient and not the universal donor

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows that even group O negative blood is given as a cross matched unit whenever there is time, because the label universal donor does not remove the need for the matching test

question: The unit of pressure in the SI system is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. pascal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pressure is force on a unit of area and its unit is the pascal, which is one newton on one square metre

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — watt: The watt is the unit of power

B — joule: The joule is the unit of energy and work

D — newton: The newton is the unit of force

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse understands why a wide blood pressure cuff gives a wrong low reading, because the pressure on the arm depends on the force spread over the area of the cuff

question: The chief function of the platelets in the blood is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. help in the clotting of blood

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The platelets stick to the injured vessel wall and help to form the clot that stops the bleeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — fight infection: Infection is fought by the white cells

C — carry oxygen: Oxygen is carried by the red cells

D — carry food to the tissues: Food is carried in the plasma

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse looks at the platelet count before a procedure and watches the puncture site for oozing, because a low count turns a simple injection into a long bleed

question: The part of the ear that helps to maintain the balance of the body is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. semicircular canals

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The semicircular canals are filled with fluid and tell the brain about the position and the movement of the head

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ear drum: The ear drum passes the sound inwards

B — auditory nerve: The auditory nerve carries the sound to the brain

C — cochlea: The cochlea is the organ of hearing

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse understands why a patient with a head injury and giddiness is walked with support, because the balance organ has been disturbed and the patient may fall without warning

question: A patient is ordered two tablets of 500 mg each. The total dose in grams is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1 g

🧠 Method: Two tablets of 500 mg give 1,000 mg, and 1,000 mg is one gram

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 2 g: Two grams would be four tablets

C — 1.5 g: One and a half grams would be three tablets

D — 0.5 g: Half a gram would be one tablet only

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Convert the milligrams into grams before writing the total on the chart, because a dose written as 1,000 mg is the one that is later misread as one tablet

question: In a hospital of 240 nurses, 25 per cent are on night duty. The number on night duty is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 60

🧠 Method: One quarter of 240 is 60, so sixty nurses are on night duty

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 72: 72 would be thirty per cent

C — 96: 96 would be forty per cent

D — 48: 48 would be twenty per cent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Take ten per cent of the number first and build the answer from it, because ten per cent of any number is found by moving the decimal point one place

question: A patient's 24-hour urine collection measures 1,800 mL. The average output in each hour is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 75 mL

🧠 Method: One thousand eight hundred millilitres divided by twenty four hours gives 75 mL in each hour

🔍 Key Clues: 800 mL

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 45 mL: 45 mL an hour would give 1,080 mL in a day

B — 90 mL: 90 mL an hour would give 2,160 mL

C — 60 mL: 60 mL an hour would give 1,440 mL

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Divide the total by twenty four and compare it with the hourly chart, because a patient who passes a large volume in the day and almost nothing at night still averages normal while the kidney is failing

question: A nurse works eight hours a day for six days and earns 9,600 rupees. The wage for each hour is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 200 rupees

🧠 Method: The total hours are forty eight, and 9,600 divided by 48 gives 200 rupees an hour

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 150 rupees: 150 rupees an hour would give only 7,200 rupees

C — 240 rupees: 240 rupees an hour would give 11,520 rupees

D — 300 rupees: 300 rupees an hour would give 14,400 rupees

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Find the total number of hours first, because dividing the wage by the days instead of the hours gives a figure that has no meaning at all

question: If 15 is subtracted from a number, the result is 27. The number is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 42

🧠 Method: The number is the result plus the amount subtracted, so 27 plus 15 gives 42

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 52: 52 is ten more than the required number

C — 12: 12 is the difference between fifteen and twenty seven

D — 32: 32 is twenty seven plus five

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Read the words again and write them as a small equation, because in these questions the operation that the words suggest is often the opposite of the one written

question: A bottle of 500 mL of fluid contains 25 g of a drug. The strength of the solution is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 5 per cent

🧠 Method: Twenty five grams in five hundred millilitres means five grams in each hundred millilitres, which is a five per cent solution

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 25 per cent: Twenty five per cent would hold 125 g in 500 mL

B — 2 per cent: Two per cent would hold only 10 g in 500 mL

D — 10 per cent: Ten per cent would hold 50 g in 500 mL

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Work the strength out for one hundred millilitres, because the percentage of a solution is always the amount in each hundred millilitres whatever the size of the bottle

question: The first term of the ratio 3 : 4 expressed as a percentage of the second term is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 75 per cent

🧠 Method: The first term as a fraction of the second is three quarters, and three quarters of a hundred is seventy five per cent

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 133.3 per cent: 133.3 per cent is wrong because the first term is smaller than the second

C — 25 per cent: 25 per cent is the part by which the first term falls short of the second

D — 33.3 per cent: 33.3 per cent is the second term expressed as a percentage of the first

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Note which term is asked about and which is the base, because reversing the two is the commonest error in a ratio asked as a percentage

question: Book is to read as food is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. eat

🧠 Method: A book is meant to be read and food is meant to be eaten, so the pair is the thing and its natural use

⚡ Fast Approach: State the relationship in words first, then look for the same relationship.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — kitchen: A kitchen is the place where food is prepared

C — plate: A plate is what the food is served on

D — cook: Cooking is done to the food before it is used and is not its natural use in this pair

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Take the first pair and make a sentence of it, then try the same sentence with each option, because a sentence that reads naturally is nearly always the right pair

question: Find the odd one out: 4, 8, 15, 16.
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 15

🧠 Method: Four, eight and sixteen can all be divided by four and are powers of two, while fifteen is neither

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 16: Sixteen is a multiple of four

C — 4: Four is a multiple of four

D — 8: Eight is a multiple of four

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Test each number against the property you suspect instead of judging by the way the numbers look, because a list often has more than one pattern and only one option breaks all of them

question: If CAT is written as 3-1-20, then DOG is written as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 4-15-7

🧠 Method: Each letter is replaced by its position in the alphabet, so D is 4, O is 15 and G is 7

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 4-15-6: 6 would stand for F and not for G

C — 4-14-7: 14 would stand for N and not for O

D — 5-15-7: 5 would stand for E and not for D

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Write the alphabet with the numbers under the letters once on the rough sheet, because counting the position of the letters fresh for each question is where the slips begin

question: Complete the series: B, D, F, H, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. J

🧠 Method: Every letter is two steps ahead of the one before it, so after H comes J

⚡ Fast Approach: Number the letters A=1 to Z=26 and work with numbers instead of letters.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — I: I would be only one step ahead of H

B — L: L would skip both I and J

D — K: K would skip J

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Write the letters with a small gap between them so that no letter is missed by the eye, because in a series of alternate letters the answer is often written one letter too early or too late

question: A nurse walks 200 metres towards the east and then turns left and walks 100 metres. She is now facing:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. north

🧠 Method: Walking east and turning left brings her to face the north, and the distances do not change the direction she faces

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — west: West is the turn in the opposite direction

B — east: She was facing east before the turn

C — south: South is the right turn from the east

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Read whether the question asks for the direction faced or the distance from the start, because the two are quite different and the whole answer depends on which one is asked

question: In a queue of 30 patients, one patient is twelfth from the front. His position from the end of the queue is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 19th

🧠 Method: The position from the end is the total plus one minus the position from the front, so 30 plus 1 minus 12 gives 19

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 17th: 17 would need a position of 14 from the front

B — 18th: 18 would need 13 from the front

C — 20th: 20 would need 11 from the front

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Remember that the two positions together count the same person twice, and add the one before subtracting

question: All drugs are chemicals. All chemicals are substances. Which conclusion follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. All drugs are substances

🧠 Method: If every drug is a chemical and every chemical is a substance, then every drug must be a substance

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — No chemical is a drug: It also contradicts the first statement

C — Some drugs are not substances: It contradicts the given statements

D — All substances are drugs: Reversing the statement does not follow, since all substances need not be drugs

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Draw two circles, the smaller inside the larger, before deciding, because a statement that is true in one direction is very often false when it is quietly reversed
